signature_checks.md_first_line: 15 files begin with a MyST anchor line '(sec-...)=' immediately followed by the H1/H2 heading, which is this pipeline's section-anchor convention and the target of every {ref}; recorded as a documented exception rather than a failure

site_build.authorship_widget: 1 anywidget node on the frontmatter page, binding both authors

forbidden_lexicon.scan_rule: case-insensitive whole-word match (optional plural) over content/*.md, content/*.yml and latex/manuscript.tex; fenced code blocks, directive option lines and inline code are excluded in the prose scan, raw counts are reported alongside so nothing is hidden by the exclusion rule

edits: 'produced using the Expert Review Orchestrator v29 pipeline' -> 'produced under the coordinator protocol of the Expert Review Pipeline'
table header 'Verdict as recorded' -> 'Outcome as recorded'
phase row label '4 Scaffold' -> '4 Section planning'
credit description 'Drafted all sections following scaffold, evidence packages, and style guide' -> '... following the section plans, evidence files, and style guide'
contribution description 'Drafted all sections from evidence packages under orchestrator constraints' -> '... from the evidence files under the coordinator protocol'
'explorer for the evidence packages underlying each section' -> 'explorer for the evidence files underlying each section'

classes.detail: 'Expert Review Orchestrator v29' and 'Scaffold Construction Protocol' are the literal titles of two shipped coordinator skills; renaming them in the auto-generated Pipeline Skills table would misreport the software actually used.

'comprev-orchestrator-v29.md' and 'comprev-scaffold.md' are the filenames in skills/ from which that table is generated; the table is a directory listing, so the tokens cannot be reworded without the row ceasing to name a real file.
inside the fenced block that reproduces the user's review request byte-for-byte (SHA256 published in provenance/review_request.md); editing it would break the hash and the provenance claim.

each occurrence corresponds 1:1 to a surviving Methods.md occurrence (4 in the auto-generated skills table, 3 in the verbatim prompt block); the three corrected files (provenance.md, authors.yml, evidence_database.md) are not assembled into the LaTeX manuscript, so regeneration from corrected content is byte-identical and the tex was left unmodified.

classes.kind: byte-verbatim user prompt with published SHA256
classes.detail: explicitly out of scope for rewriting; the file's value is that it is unaltered.
